subject: python
title: Functions & Scope
description: Defining functions, return values, default arguments, *args/**kwargs and local scope.

content.title: Definition
content.body: A function groups a piece of behaviour under a name. It runs only when you call it, and it hands a value back with return.

content.title: Scope
content.body: Names created inside a function are local: they exist while the call runs and are invisible outside it.

content.title: Good practice
content.body: Return values instead of printing them, and keep one function to one job. It makes the code testable and easy to read later.

exercises.question: What does a Python function return when it has no return statement?
exercises.explanation: Every Python function returns a value. With no explicit return, that value is None.

exercises.question: Which line breaks this function?
exercises.code:
1  def greet(name)
2      message = "Hi " + name
3      return message
4
5  print(greet("Anna"))

answers.text: Line 5 — greet must be called with a keyword
Line 1 — missing colon after the parameter list

exercises.explanation: A def header always ends with a colon: def greet(name):

exercises.question: Complete the function so it hands the sum back to the caller.
exercises.explanation: return sends the value back to the caller. print only writes to the console and returns None.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: Variables assigned inside a function have ___ scope.
exercises.explanation: Assignment inside a function creates a local name, unless you declare it global or nonlocal.

exercises.question: What is the value of counter() on the second call?
exercises.code:
def make_counter():
    n = 0
    def counter():
        nonlocal n
        n += 1
        return n
    return counter

tick = make_counter()
tick()
tick()
exercises.explanation: The inner function closes over n, so the value survives between calls. Two calls give 2.

exercises.question: *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple.
exercises.explanation: *args gathers leftover positional arguments as a tuple; **kwargs gathers keyword arguments as a dict.

exercises.question: Which keyword lets a function reassign a name defined at module level?
exercises.explanation: global targets module-level names; nonlocal targets a name in the nearest enclosing function.

exercises.question: Gotcha
exercises.back: The list is created once at definition time and shared by every call
exercises.explanation: Use bucket=None and build a fresh list inside the body. This is one of the most common Python bugs in review.
